principles: Represent adapter packs as declarative metadata, not executable lifecycle control.
Reuse the existing proof-admissibility vocabulary and registry surface instead of duplicating it.
Fail closed on duplicate ids, duplicate schemas, duplicate artifact surfaces, and unknown pack lookups.
Keep production, Authority, scientific-truth, and physical-validation claims outside local pack descriptors.
drivers: M1 must make future Quantum/PINN packs pluggable without changing gate semantics.
Existing proof-admissibility consumers must remain the source of lifecycle truth.
The smoke must prove both happy path inventory and adversarial duplicate rejection.

options.name: declarative-read-only-registry
pros: Small M1 slice with low gate risk
Creates a shared extension point for future domain packs
cons: Does not yet load external schema files

options.name: full-pack-runtime-now
pros: Would expose more future functionality immediately
Could combine schema, verifier, gate policy, and benchmark work
cons: Too broad for one lifecycle story
Risks duplicating proof manager or gate semantics
Would mix Quantum/PINN future milestones into M1

rationale: Choose the read-only declarative registry because M1 needs a safe extension contract first; schema loading, verifier execution, gate policy, and benchmarks belong in later stories.

preMortem.scenario: The pack registry becomes a second proof manager
preMortem.trigger: Registry starts storing evidence or lifecycle decisions
preMortem.mitigation: Keep registry read-only and test that no ledger/storage/gate exports are added

preMortem.scenario: Packs overclaim production or scientific truth
preMortem.trigger: Descriptor fields imply productionDone, Authority, quantum truth, or solver improvement
preMortem.mitigation: Smoke checks forbidden claim terminology and productionDone absence

preMortem.scenario: Duplicate pack surfaces cause ambiguous evaluation
preMortem.trigger: Two packs claim the same artifactKind, alias, schema id, or claim id
preMortem.consequence: Consumers cannot know which policy applies
